reviewBoundary: Three new complete junior1 ten-gap three-choice narratives, using the recorded whole-passage task format. Author checks contextual keys and both distractors; option positions shuffled before freeze. Fictional events, not independent learner calibration or a claim of specialised dog-training advice.

materials.title: A paper crown for Grandpa
materials.text:
Grandpa's birthday was on Sunday. My little sister wanted to buy him a crown. "He tells the best stories," she said. "He should be a ____1____."

We went to a toy shop, but every crown was too small. My sister looked ____2____. Then I remembered the large sheet of gold paper at home. Perhaps we could make one.

We measured Grandpa's old hat to find the right ____3____. I drew a long strip, and my sister added stars. We cut it out and joined the ends with tape. The crown looked beautiful, but it fell over when we put it on the table. The paper was too ____4____.

Mum suggested putting a strip of card inside. This made the crown ____5____ enough to stand. My sister wanted to cover it with more stars, but we left a small space at the front for a ____6____: "Our Story King."

On Sunday, Grandpa opened our box. He put the crown on and laughed. It was larger than a toy crown, but it ____7____ him perfectly.

After tea, we asked for a story. Grandpa began, "Once there were two clever children who made something with their own ____8____."

My sister smiled. The crown had cost almost nothing, but Grandpa kept it on all afternoon. Later, he put it on his bookshelf, ____9____ his favourite storybook. When we visited the next week, it was still there. We had not found the right present in a shop. We had ____10____ it together.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: A crown and the later title Story King establish king. Driver and doctor do not match the crown idea.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: No crown fits Grandpa, so she is disappointed. Excitement would fit success, and no cue supports sleepiness.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Measuring his hat finds the head size needed. Price and colour are not found by measuring the hat.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Paper that cannot stand needs support because it is thin. Cleanliness and brightness do not explain collapse.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Card makes the crown strong enough to stand. Quiet is irrelevant and heavy does not specify resistance to bending.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Our Story King is a written message. It is not a button or flower.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The measured crown fits him perfectly. Missed and followed do not describe wearing a correctly sized crown.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: They make the crown with their hands. Eyes help see but do not perform the construction, and feet do not do the craft.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: A crown on a shelf can stand beside a storybook. Under or inside the book conflicts with the displayed standing crown.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: They make the present together. It is neither lost nor borrowed from another owner.

materials.title: The picnic place
materials.text:
We planned a bicycle picnic beside the lake. On Saturday morning, the sky was clear. Dad packed sandwiches, and I put apples in a bag. My sister brought a small ____1____ so we could sit on the grass.

Halfway to the lake, dark clouds appeared. Then rain began to fall. We left the road and stopped at an empty bus shelter. Its roof kept us ____2____, but we could not continue our ride immediately.

I was angry with the weather. "The day is ____3____," I said.

Dad looked at his watch. It was nearly lunchtime. "The lake will still be there another day," he said. "The sandwiches are here ____4____."

We sat on the bench and opened the food. My sister spread her cloth over our knees like a tiny table. A woman waiting for the bus smiled at us. We offered her an apple, and she showed us a photograph of the lake in ____5____. The water was frozen, and snow covered the path.

"I've only seen it in summer," I said. Her picture made me want to ____6____ again in another season.

After lunch, the rain stopped. We checked the road and decided to ride ____7____ instead of continuing to the lake. There would be enough time to dry our clothes before visiting Grandma.

At home, my sister drew our picnic. She included the shelter, bench and woman with the photograph. The lake was not in the picture, but our day was. I had thought a good picnic needed one ____8____ place. Now I knew it also needed food and people I enjoyed being ____9____. We would try the lake again, but I did not want to ____10____ the picnic we had already had.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The later spread cloth is what she brought for sitting on grass. Camera and umbrella do not match that item.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A roof shelters them from rain and keeps them dry. Cold and late are not protection from rain.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Anger about rain makes the narrator call the day ruined. Sunny contradicts the rain, and planned does not express the negative judgment.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Dad contrasts a future visit with sandwiches available now. Yesterday is past, and outside does not express the present timing.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Frozen water and snow establish winter. Spring and autumn are not the season indicated by these cues.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: Seeing a different season prompts another visit to the lake. Cooking and waiting do not describe going there again.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: They return home to dry clothes before Grandma's visit. Uphill gives no destination and abroad invents foreign travel.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: The narrator had made a successful picnic depend on the planned special lakeside place. Strange and secret are not features of the originally chosen public lake.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: Enjoy being with people expresses pleasant company. Against opposition and under position do not fit that meaning.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The drawing preserves a real picnic the narrator does not want to forget. Measuring is unrelated, and an event already experienced cannot now be cancelled.

materials.title: Pip and the blue glove
materials.text:
My aunt's dog Pip liked carrying things. He brought slippers to the door and sometimes took a newspaper into the garden. When Aunt May said he could help find lost things, I wanted to ____1____ him.

I placed a blue glove behind a chair while Pip waited in the kitchen. Then Aunt May let him smell its partner. He ran into the room, looked around and returned with a ____2____. It was blue too, but it belonged on my foot.

I laughed. "He has found the wrong thing!"

Aunt May did not call him a bad dog. She took the sock gently and showed him the glove again. "We need to make the task ____3____," she said.

This time, I placed the glove where part of it was ____4____ beside the chair. Pip found it quickly. We praised him and stopped after a few short tries, before he became ____5____.

Later, I could not find my own cap. I almost called Pip, but the garden gate was open and a delivery van was outside. Aunt May asked me to keep Pip ____6____ while she closed the gate. A game did not matter more than keeping him safe.

I found the cap myself, ____7____ the newspaper. Pip had not hidden it; I had put the paper on top of it.

That afternoon taught me two things. Helping a dog learn required ____8____, not just a loud command. And before blaming someone else for a lost object, I should ____9____ where I had left it. Pip carried his toy to me, and I put away my notebook. Nothing was missing now; we could simply ____10____.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator wants to test the claimed finding skill. Washing or selling Pip does not check it.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 2.
questions.explanation: A blue item worn on the foot is a sock. Hat goes on the head and glove on the hand.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 3.
questions.explanation: Showing the glove again and making it partly visible clarifies the task. Longer and noisier do not specify the helpful change.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 4.
questions.explanation: A visible part helps Pip spot the glove. Wetness and weight do not improve the visual cue described.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Short practice ends before fatigue. Fame and wealth are not possible states relevant to the dog's session.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 6.
questions.explanation: An open gate and van mean Pip should stay inside until the gate is shut. Outside increases the problem and sleep is not the instruction.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 7.
questions.explanation: The paper had been placed on top of the cap, so the cap is under it. Above and beside contradict the stated covering.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 8.
questions.explanation: Gentle repetition, praise and short practice show patience. No payment is involved; complete silence contradicts guidance and praise.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 9.
questions.explanation: The narrator should check their own actions before blaming another. Hiding or announcing a location does not establish where the object actually is.

questions.prompt: Choose the best word or phrase for blank 10.
questions.explanation: The toy invites them to play together. Nothing needs searching for, and no delivery task is waiting.
